rationale: Round 6, lens: AC falsifiability and internal consistency, re-read from disk at 8b3a5535. All 4 of my round-5 asks are ADDRESSED: the residual now states that F2 reads untracked, agent-writable panel.json while only F1/F3/F4 are git-derived, the panel-edit reach is pinned by AC-11 (ix-g), and the bead-side anchor tightening is correctly declared subsumed (with anchors gone, a forged high-round registration cannot neutralise anything; only deletion/rewrite can, and that is stated); the single-directory legs (vii-s) and (i-a) exercise the real in-place convention; Q's duplicate-epic order is pinned and N2a's P is non-epic; OQ-9 is qualified and OQ-10 deferred. The diff is a tightening, not a regression: removing round comparison removes the one input an attacker chose freely, and the (x-c)/(x-a)/(x-m)/(ix-g)/(i-m)/(i-c) legs each bind to one named branch of F1–F5 or the validity contract. On the Round-6 question I checked the pre-complete gate: internal/panel/gate.go (6) blocks `complete` unless reviewed_head_sha EQUALS the pre-materialization bead HEAD (exact, line 280), and complete.go runs the gate before materialization so the reviewed SHA is always an ancestor of the landing's second parent. Therefore a normal bead — one round complete-landed, a fix round re-panelled in place, or complete's own later commits — can never carry an outside-tip registration, and F2 never refuses it; #239 still recovers through reattest ((i), (i-a), (i-c)). The only landed beads F2 can refuse are those with a SECOND registration the gate never matched: an abandoned registration (gate rule (3) allows it before the staleness check) or a second slug/ad-hoc panel whose SHA was rebased away — both are recorded exceptional exits, the spec states them ((x-a), (x-c)) with the override exit, and under the measured convention (zero -r* dirs) neither is normal. Two minor pins remain: F2's treatment of an EMPTY reviewed_head_sha is undefined while R4.3's set semantics skip empties; and the plan-source rule does not say what happens when spec/<S> exists but the plan.md blob is absent on it. Approve with asks.
concrete_changes_required: R4.2 F2 provenance gate: define the EMPTY reviewed_head_sha case. R4.3's set semantics take 'every non-empty reviewed_head_sha' (today's reviewedHeadSHAForBead skips empties), while F2 says a value that fails wellFormedGitObjectID makes the registration MALFORMED and F2 fails closed; an empty string fails that gate. Pin one behaviour (recommend: an empty SHA is skipped by F2 exactly as R4.3 skips it, because it is 'no review recorded', not an unlanded review) and add it to (x-m) or a sibling leg.

R1.1 (c) Source: state the case where the branch spec/<S> exists but `spec/<S>:<path>/plan.md` is absent on it (plan drafted in the worktree, not yet committed, or a spec whose plan lives only in the checkout). As written, 'the committed blob whenever spec/<S> exists, otherwise the checkout' and 'absent in both places → all N4' leave that case between two rules. Recommend: branch exists but blob absent → use the checkout file (and print the divergence notice only when both exist and differ); pin it in the AC-1 fixtures.

findings.title: Round-6 question: 'any outside-tip registration refuses' never refuses a normal bead, and #239 still recovers
findings.detail: Evidence from the tree: internal/panel/gate.go rule (6) 'stale SHA → Block' compares p.ReviewedHeadSHA with the bead's HEAD by exact equality (line 280), and internal/complete/complete.go runs that gate BEFORE materialization ('the gate measures the PRE-materialization beadHead tip'), after which complete's own commits (materialization, JSONL sync) advance the tip to the second parent. So for any bead that landed through `complete`, the matched registration's reviewed SHA is an ancestor of the second parent, hence of the landing merge, hence of the spec tip whenever the merge is reachable — which is the only case the fallback admits. Normal shapes: (1) one round, complete-landed → in tip history, passes; (2) a fix round after the panel → either re-panelled in place (SHA bumped to the new tip, which the gate then requires) or NOT re-panelled, in which case the gate blocks `complete` and the bead never lands; (3) complete's later commits → #233's shape, the SHA is an ancestor, passes (i-c). Shapes F2 does refuse: (a) an ABANDONED registration — gate rule (3) 'abandoned → Allow + Warn, BEFORE staleness' lets the bead land with a stale SHA in that dir, and F2 then refuses it (x-a): a recorded exceptional exit, not a normal bead; (b) a second registration directory for the same bead (the `-r2` slug or an ad-hoc panel) that the gate did not match and whose SHA was rebased away (x-c) — absent in the measured convention (zero -r* dirs). Both refusals name the directory and the override exit. #239 recovery: (i), (i-a), (i-c) accept via reattest; the read-back re-runs F2 at read time, so a later NEW registration outside the tip ((xv)) un-accepts it until re-vouched — consistent with the finder-only ruling.

findings.title: F2 and R4.3 disagree on an empty reviewed_head_sha
findings.detail: R4.3: 'every non-empty reviewed_head_sha across all registrations' (today's reviewedHeadSHAForBead also skips empties). R4.2 F2: a value that does not pass wellFormedGitObjectID is MALFORMED and F2 fails closed; an empty string does not pass that gate. A registration with an empty SHA (a `panel create` whose --target could not be resolved, or a hand-written file) would therefore be ignored by R4.3 and refuse under F2. Pin one rule and a leg.

findings.title: Plan source rule has a gap: branch exists, blob absent
findings.detail: R1.1 (c): 'The committed spec/<S>:<path> blob … whenever spec/<S> exists. Otherwise, the invoking checkout's … plan.md' and 'If plan.md is absent in both places, no N is mapped'. When spec/<S> exists but has no committed plan.md (worktree-drafted, uncommitted), the first rule selects a non-existent blob and the second does not apply because the checkout file exists. The intended behaviour (fall through to the checkout file) should be written and pinned.

findings.title: Verified against 8b3a5535 / live tree (no change needed)
findings.detail: Regression check of `git diff 7404845f 8b3a5535`: F2 is strictly stronger than the round-5 rule (every round-5 refusal is still a refusal; the only new passes are shapes with no outside-tip registration, (i-a) single-dir and (i-c)); the anchor machinery, ties and missing-round branches are gone and nothing else references them; (x-t) is replaced by (x-c)/(x-a)/(x-m), each binding to one branch (cross-dir rounds irrelevant; abandoned outside-tip refuses; malformed SHA fails closed before any git operand). q9ea's removal from the fallback exits is consistent: restoring bead/<id> at the second parent satisfies only F3 and the fallback never identifies from a tip. The validity-qualified no-op ((i-m)) is consistent with the read-back's VALID requirement. The corroboration provenance string lets a JSONL inspector distinguish fallback acceptances. PlanMapsBead counting 'exactly as extractBeadSectionRaw does, fenced lines included' removes the one way selection and MF-1 could disagree, and the fenced-heading pin is named. The lazy-read trigger (every plan-form row not already N2a/N2c) matches the classification order (N4 before N2b/N1) and keeps AC-4 (iv) at zero reads. The 9–12 bead estimate is consistent with OQ-1's per-requirement breakdown. AC-12 (iv) no longer assumes tree identity, matching the F2 '#233's shape' text. The ix-g characterisation leg is correctly labelled as pinning a documented reach rather than red-on-revert.
